metadata.Name: JCoLA
metadata.Description: JCoLA is a Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability consisting of 10,020 sentences annotated with binary acceptability judgments.
metadata.Paper Title: JCoLA: Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability
metadata.Abstract: This paper introduces JCoLA (Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability), a dataset for evaluating the syntactic knowledge of Japanese language models. JCoLA consists of 10,020 sentences with binary acceptability judgments, extracted from linguistics textbooks, handbooks, and journal articles. The dataset is split into in-domain and out-of-domain data, with the latter categorized by 12 linguistic phenomena. The paper evaluates the performance of various Japanese and multilingual language models on JCoLA, demonstrating that while some models surpass human performance on in-domain data, none exceed human performance on out-of-domain data.
